name: PICA and lateral medullary territory
summary: The dorsolateral medulla and the inferior cerebellum perfused by the posterior inferior cerebellar artery and the small lateral medullary branches of the vertebral artery. It is the anatomical substrate of the Wallenberg syndrome and of the inferior cerebellar infarct that swells against the fourth ventricle.

anatomy.location: Dorsolateral quadrant of the medulla at the level of the inferior olive (spinothalamic tract, spinal trigeminal nucleus and tract, nucleus ambiguus, vestibular nuclei, inferior cerebellar peduncle, descending sympathetic fibers); the inferior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere, the tonsil and the inferior vermis.

function: Pain and temperature relay for the body and face, swallowing and phonation, vestibular processing, sympathetic outflow to the head and cerebellar coordination of the ipsilateral limbs.

bloodSupply.note: Territory boundaries in this atlas come from a probabilistic stroke-lesion atlas (Liu et al. 2023) and shift between individuals with the anatomy of the circle of Willis.

bestView.label: dorsolateral medulla at the inferior olive

imaging.normalAppearance: The lateral half of the medulla behind the olive on axial slices and the cerebellum below the horizontal fissure; on coronal slices the territory runs from the tonsil up to the inferior vermis.

pathology.finding: Small area of restricted diffusion in the dorsolateral medulla; often subtle and best seen on thin axial and coronal DWI.
Diffusion restriction of the inferior cerebellar hemisphere and tonsil, with swelling that can obliterate the fourth ventricle.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Thin-slice DWI; CTA of the vertebral arteries; serial CT if drowsy

lesionEffects.mechanism: Spinal trigeminal tract (face) and crossed spinothalamic tract (body)

pearls: No weakness, crossed sensory loss, dysphagia and Horner: the lateral medulla
Vertebral dissection is the cause to look for in the young
